answer: Before filing, the filer must wander a route carrying a walnut-shell signal lamp, stopping at three checkpoints where neighbours record the signal. The desk checks the town book within a day: the lamp must have been seen at three checkpoints by three different witnesses, proving the filer visited real sites instead of filing from one desk. Fewer than three witnesses, or one witness twice, means rejection and the 250-coin bond forfeited, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real routes plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims on one route; all forty fell when the witnesses had seen him once.
